title: Authorize Architect A non-destructive move-out restoration assessment (exclude kitchen-water)
fixedRequirements: Keep kitchen-water work separate from the move-out restoration assessment.
rationale: Move-out walk-through reported multiple physical deficiencies plus a potential immediate safety concern at the SE bedroom loft-ladder railing (Move-out inspection, document:14668b...). Repair methods, quantities, and pricing are not yet defined and some conditions may be pre-existing per the condition/maintenance history (document:5c1f63...). Architect A’s non-destructive assessment is the direct next step to define a practical restoration scope and preliminary budget without commencing repairs, without destructive investigation/testing/permitting, and without any resident-liability determination (Restoration assessment service, document:9be1a8..., and quote, document:97bac...). This preserves the explicit requirement to keep kitchen-water separate (Owner instructions, document:e8f41d...). Funding for exactly this assessment amount is evidenced as allocated by Company A (Owner work funds, document:f102cb...).
scope: Non-destructive site visit (up to 3 hours) to inspect reported move-out deficiencies and note immediate safety concerns; exclude any kitchen-water investigation/repairs; observe the SE bedroom loft-ladder railing area only from a safe position with no contact/leaning.

Room-by-room condition and photographic/quantity schedule based on what is actually observed and measured at the visit; clearly distinguish observed/measured items from missing or unavailable supporting materials (e.g., missing arrival-condition photos).

Written restoration scope and preliminary budget note: practical repair approaches; unknowns; identify items needing specialist trade quotes; flag immediate safety concerns; exclude repairs, destructive investigation, testing, permitting, and any resident-liability determination; keep kitchen-water out of scope.
